tools.description:
Check a btw program without playing it: parse, type-check and compile the text. ALWAYS call check before eval, share or render, and fix every error at its line:col before trying again: a program with an error is refused whole. Warnings do not block.

Answers {ok, errors, warnings, diagnostics[{severity, line, col, end_col, message, expected, found, help, render}], cid, canonical, tempo, key, sections, song_bars, seconds, evolve, uses_assets, restricted}. line and col are 1-based; help says what would fix it ("did you mean ..."); render is the same error in caret form. ok:false is an answer, not a tool error. cid and canonical are of the canonical text (comments and spacing do not change the CID).

With same_as (another program's CID or text) the answer gains same_as {same, text_same, basis, why, diffs[{section, deck, start_bar, a_cid, b_cid}], only_in_a, only_in_b, renamed, song, diff}: whether the two are the same song by their compiled nets and song-level settings, not their text. When they are not, diff says what changed in music: diff.summary is one line per change ("tempo 124 -> 126", "moved outro: bar 13 -> bar 5", "drop2 bass = drop bass transposed +1", "drop bass: 1 note changed (1:7 c3 -> d3)"), with song, arrangement (inserted, removed, moved, repeated, renamed, changed) and parts (a transform: transpose, octave, rotate, reverse, thin, fill, fast, slow; else the notes added, removed or changed at bar:step) as JSON. Use it to prove a refactor changed nothing, or to find what an edit did.

Voices come from the instruments tool; the grammar is https://btw.bitwrap.io/docs/cheatsheet.md. Read-only, no sign-in. Limits: the text is at most 16384 bytes; about 60 calls a minute.

same_as.description: Optional: another program to compare with, as its CID (stored here, or an example's), a short https://btw.bitwrap.io/p/<CID> link, or its text. The answer gains same_as: whether the two are the same song by their compiled nets and song-level settings (tempo, key, swing, length, end, loop), not their text: a let/def/repeat refactor or a renamed section is the same song; a changed note is not, and diff says what changed in music (song settings, sections moved or inserted, a part transposed or rotated, notes at bar:step).

text.description: The program text (at most 16384 bytes). Comments and blank lines are fine.

tools.name: check

annotations.title: Compose a program from a prompt

tools.description:
Write a whole btw music program from a prompt with a language model, and get it back already checked: the canonical program text, its CID, the check report, the attempts the repair loop needed, a render_url (audio) and a share_url (link). Needs a bearer token (sign in on https://btw.bitwrap.io, "MCP token").

It takes 5 to 60 seconds, up to about 90 when the first drafts had errors and the server repaired them (up to 3 rounds); do not call it again while it runs. It is rate limited per user (currently 10 per hour and 50 per day per user) and per address, and the site has a daily spend cap: on rate_limited wait retry_after seconds and tell the user; on spend_cap, disabled or not_configured stop and say so; on unrepairable the details hold the last diagnostics, so adjust the prompt (simpler, or give a base_cid) rather than repeating it.

The result is stored publicly under CC0-1.0 (public domain): never put anything private in the prompt. Pass base_cid (an example's CID, or a program compose or render stored) to edit that program instead of starting from nothing. To hear it: render (audio at stream_url), or eval / load into a browser tab.

base_cid.description: Optional CID of a public program (an example or one the site stored) to edit instead of starting fresh; the result records it as forked from.

genre.description: Optional genre hint, e.g. dubstep, trance, techno, ambient.

key.description: Optional key, as the language writes it: am, c, f#m, d:dorian, d:phrygian.

length.description: Optional: short, medium, long, or a number of bars (at most 256).

prompt.description: What to write, in plain words: mood, genre, instruments, structure, e.g. "dark techno at 128 with an acid line and a long breakdown". At most 800 characters.

tools.name: compose

tools.description:
List the phones paired with the token's account (djrust on Android scans the QR code that https://btw.bitwrap.io shows under Phone; btwsite/PAIRING.md): id, name, fingerprint (the code both ends showed at pairing), paired, connected (djrust has its stream open now), last_seen, and state (what it last reported: cid, playing, section, bar). Pairing is the grant: a phone paired by an account is driven over MCP with that account's token and no other.

Pass a phone's id as device to eval, load, get or stop to drive that phone alone (eval and load run the same checks as for a tab; a program with errors, samples or "use restricted" is not sent). Needs a bearer token. Read-only.
tools.name: devices

annotations.title: Play a program in a browser tab

tools.description:
Send a program to a browser tab that has https://btw.bitwrap.io open, as if the user pressed Cmd+Enter in the editor: the text replaces the editor's and the change lands on the next bar, with no gap; play:true starts playback too. Needs a bearer token.

A tab must be connected. It is the page's own connection, so ask the user to open https://btw.bitwrap.io in a browser (signed in as the same account as the token, and eval reaches every live tab of that account), or, for a tab that is not signed in, to press MCP in the page's top bar and give you the session id it shows, which you pass as session. With no tab connected the answer is a no_session error that says this.

Run check first. eval checks too and refuses a program with errors (nothing is sent; the diagnostics come back), and one that uses samples or "use restricted" (the browser has no such files). The program is the user's to hear: do not eval over something they are playing without saying so. After eval call get to see what is playing, the section and bar, and any diagnostics the page itself reports. Text is at most 16384 bytes.

device.description: Id of one of your paired phones (djrust on Android), from the devices tool. Targets that phone alone; do not combine with session.

play.description: Start playing too (default false: load it and leave it stopped, or leave a playing tab as it is).

session.description: Session id of one browser tab, from the MCP panel of the page. Leave out to use your own signed-in tabs (every live one for eval/load/stop, the latest for get).

text.description: The program text. It must pass check.

tools.name: eval

tools.description: Rewrite a btw program in its canonical form (one statement a line, one space between tokens, blocks indented two spaces, numbers, notes and chords spelled one way, comments dropped) and return the text with its CID and the comments it dropped. The CID is of the canonical text, so formatting never changes it: use fmt to compare two programs or to show a tidy listing. A program that does not parse answers the same diagnostics as check. Read-only, no sign-in.
tools.name: fmt

annotations.title: What a browser tab is playing

tools.description:
What a browser tab at https://btw.bitwrap.io is doing now, as the page last reported it: the program text and cid, playing (true/false), source (engine or stream), section (name), section_num of sections_total, bar, bars_in_section, phase (0-7, the light in the phrase), marks (what is firing: active lines, token flashes, ramps and timed lines, with line:col spans into the text), diagnostics (the page's own check of the text), and ts. Use it after eval or load to confirm the change landed, and to see the program a user is playing and editing.

Needs a bearer token: it reads the tabs of the token's account, by default the most recently seen one. A tab that is not signed in is read by its session id (the page's MCP panel shows it), with your token. Read-only. No tab connected: a no_session error that says how to connect one.

device.description: Id of one of your paired phones (djrust on Android), from the devices tool. Targets that phone alone; do not combine with session.

session.description: Session id of one browser tab, from the MCP panel of the page. Leave out to use your own signed-in tabs (every live one for eval/load/stop, the latest for get).

tools.name: get

tools.description: The sounds a program may name: voices (inst=NAME), families (a name that contains one plays that family's generic voice and check warns about it), drum kits (kit=NAME) and palettes. Use only names from this answer: an unknown inst= is a check error with the nearest names. Read-only, no sign-in, cached for five minutes.
tools.name: instruments

tools.description: The public example programs of https://btw.bitwrap.io, all CC0-1.0: name, title, description, cid, bpm, bars, license and the url of the raw .btw. Pass name to get that program's full text as well. Read two or three before writing a program of your own: after the cheat-sheet (https://btw.bitwrap.io/docs/cheatsheet.md) they are the best guide to the language, from a four-line beat (first-beat) to whole tracks with sections, defs, ramps and evolve. Read-only, no sign-in.

name.description: Optional: also return this example's full text.

tools.name: list_examples

annotations.title: Load a stored program into a browser tab

tools.description: Put a stored or example program into a browser tab (the same tabs and rules as eval: a tab open at https://btw.bitwrap.io, signed in as the token's account, or its session id from the page's MCP panel). Give exactly one of: cid (a program the site stored, or an example's CID; compose and render store theirs), example (a name from list_examples), url (a share link https://btw.bitwrap.io/#CID.packed, a /c/ link or a beats.bitwrap.io/p# link; the link is verified, and one whose CID is not its text's is refused with cid_mismatch). play:true starts it. Needs a bearer token. Call get afterwards to see what is playing.

cid.description: CID of a program the site has stored (compose and render store theirs) or of an example.

device.description: Id of one of your paired phones (djrust on Android), from the devices tool. Targets that phone alone; do not combine with session.

example.description: Name of an example, from list_examples.

play.description: Start playing too (default false: load it and leave it stopped, or leave a playing tab as it is).

session.description: Session id of one browser tab, from the MCP panel of the page. Leave out to use your own signed-in tabs (every live one for eval/load/stop, the latest for get).

url.description: A share link: https://btw.bitwrap.io/#<CID>.<packed>, a /c/ link, a beats.bitwrap.io/p# link, or a short /p/<CID> link (the program must be stored here).

tools.name: load

tools.description: Decode a btw share link and return its canonical text, its CID and whether the CID verifies against the text. Takes either form: a self-sealing link (https://btw.bitwrap.io/#<CID>.<packed>, a /c/<CID>.<packed> link, a beats.bitwrap.io/p# link, a bare #fragment or <CID>.<packed>) or a CID-only link (https://btw.bitwrap.io/p/<CID>, /c/<CID>, https://beats.bitwrap.io/p/<CID>, #<CID>, or a bare CID), which is resolved from the programs the site has stored (shared signed in, composed or rendered) and the examples, and answers its rights in meta. Either way the text is recompiled and its CID recomputed: a program whose CID is not its text's is refused with cid_mismatch, and an unknown CID answers not_found. Do not trust or play a refused text. Comments carried in a link (notes) are unverified. Read-only, no sign-in.

url.description: A share link (self-sealing #<CID>.<packed>, or a short <site>/p/<CID> or /c/<CID> link), a #fragment, <CID>.<packed>, or a bare CID.

tools.name: open

annotations.title: Up next: queue programs on a browser tab

tools.description:
An "up next" queue on one browser tab at https://btw.bitwrap.io (the same tabs and rules as load: session, or device, else your most recently seen signed-in tab). When the playing program ends the page plays the next item, on the bar line where it can; a looping program (one that never ends) plays for the item's bars or minutes, else one full pass of its arrangement, and then advances. Needs a bearer token.

action is one of: list (the queue, now_playing, position, paused_reason, listener), add (items: up to 20 per call, 50 in the queue), remove (item: an item id from list, or a CID), clear, skip (play the next item now).

Items must already be programs: {cid} of a stored program (compose, render and share store theirs) or an example's CID, {example} by name from list_examples, or {url} a share link (verified exactly as load verifies it; a CID-only link must name a stored program). Optional per item: bars (1-1024) or minutes (0.1-120) to play, title. THE QUEUE NEVER COMPOSES OR CALLS A MODEL, and there is no way to make it: to queue generated music, call compose yourself (it is rate limited and spend-capped), then add the CIDs it returns. Do not loop compose to keep a queue full.

The queue advances only while a listener is plausibly present, as the page reports it: it pauses at the next track boundary when the tab's audio is suspended, when the tab has been hidden with no key, pointer, touch or media key for 30 minutes, or after 8 tracks in a row without any interaction; the page then shows "Still listening? Press play to continue". Only a person on the page lifts a pause: skip is refused while paused (paused_reason says why), and load still plays one program as it always has but does not resume the queue. Writes are limited to about 30 a minute. The queue lives with the tab's session and is gone when the tab is.

action.description: list, add, remove, clear or skip.

device.description: Id of one of your paired phones (djrust on Android), from the devices tool. Targets that phone alone; do not combine with session.

item.description: remove: an item id from list (q1, q2, ...) or a CID (the first queued item with it).

items.description: add: the programs to append, each an object with exactly one of cid, example, url, and optionally bars, minutes, title.

bars.description: Play this many bars, then advance (else until the program ends; a loop: one arrangement pass).

cid.description: CID of a stored program or an example.

example.description: Name of an example, from list_examples.

minutes.description: Play this long, then advance at the next bar line. Not with bars.

title.description: What the page shows for it (else the program's name).

url.description: A share link, verified as load verifies it.

session.description: Session id of one browser tab, from the MCP panel of the page. Leave out to use your own signed-in tabs (every live one for eval/load/stop, the latest for get).

tools.name: queue

tools.description: Set up a demo recording of a program: the page in record mode (full screen code, the firing markers and follow-scroll on) and the steps that turn it into a video. Give exactly one of text, cid or example (as render does: a text or example is checked and stored publicly as CC0-1.0, nothing private). Answers {cid, seconds, record_url, record_url_manual_clock, audio_url, recipe}. record_url opens the page in record mode and plays it for a person to screen-record; record_url_manual_clock opens it on a fake clock that a script steps frame by frame (window.__btw.setTime(seconds); window.__btw.frame()), which is how btwsite/tools/record-demo.mjs in the repo makes a perfectly synced, stutter-free MP4 (H.264, AAC, 1920x1080) plus a silent hero loop (MP4 and WebM) and a poster PNG, taking the audio from audio_url (the offline render of the same program). This tool does not capture video itself: it needs a browser and ffmpeg on your side. The audio is the offline render: notes and sounds, not control lines (filters, reverb). Call check first. Rendering limits apply (about 30 programs an hour per client). No sign-in needed.

cid.description: CID of a program already stored (for instance the cid compose returned).

example.description: Name of an example, from list_examples.

text.description: The program text. It must pass check; it is stored publicly (CC0-1.0).

tools.name: record

annotations.title: Render a program to streaming audio

tools.description:
Make a program streamable as audio. Give exactly one of text (the program), cid (a program already stored, e.g. what compose returned) or example (a name from list_examples). A text or example is checked, then stored publicly under its CID as CC0-1.0 if it is not stored yet (never submit anything private; programs that use samples or "use restricted" are refused). Answers {cid, stream_url, status_url, seconds, format}: open stream_url to listen (it streams the offline render as it renders; the first sound comes within about a second, so a client can play it at once), download the same URL for a file, and read status_url to see how far a render is. format is opus (Ogg Opus, small) or wav (16-bit stereo, plays chunk by chunk in a web page); default opus.

Call check first. The offline render plays the notes and sounds, not control lines (filters, reverb, do ... lines), so it can sound plainer than the browser; a program with no end (no sections or end line) is cut at the server's bar limit (256 bars). Rendering is limited per address per hour and to a few at once: on busy or rate_limited wait retry_after seconds. No sign-in needed; about 30 programs an hour per client.

cid.description: CID of a program already stored (for instance the cid compose returned).

example.description: Name of an example, from list_examples.

format.description: opus (Ogg Opus, smaller, for download or <audio>) or wav (16-bit stereo, plays chunk by chunk in a web page).

text.description: The program text. It must pass check; it is stored publicly (CC0-1.0).

tools.name: render

tools.description: Make the share links of a program. Always the self-sealing link: https://btw.bitwrap.io/#<CID>.<base64url(deflate(canonical text))>; the program travels inside the link, and whoever opens it gets exactly that text, verified against the CID, and can play and fork it. Also social_url (https://btw.bitwrap.io/c/<CID>.<packed>, the form to post where a link preview is wanted: it carries a card image) and the same link on beats.bitwrap.io. Called signed in (a bearer token), it also stores the program on the site (public, with its rights: license, forked_from, credits, name; the first share's rights stay) and returns the CID-only forms: short_url (https://btw.bitwrap.io/p/<CID>), short_social_url (https://btw.bitwrap.io/c/<CID>) and short_beats_url (https://beats.bitwrap.io/p/<CID>), plus fetch_url, a public GET that returns the canonical text and rights for a phone or an app. Opening a short link fetches the text, recompiles it, recomputes the CID and refuses a mismatch. Anonymous calls get the self-sealing links and short_url null. The program must pass check and must not use samples or "use restricted" (a private program is never shared or stored); programs shared here are CC0 unless license says otherwise. Links over about 2000 characters (chars says) may be cut by some apps; short links are not.

credits.description: Who is credited, one short line each. Stored with the rights.

forked_from.description: CID of the program this one was forked from. Stored with the rights.

license.description: Rights kept with the stored program, an SPDX-style id (default CC0-1.0). Only used when the program is stored (signed in).

name.description: A name for the program (else its `#! name:` line).

text.description: The program text. It must pass check.

tools.name: share

tools.description: Stop what a browser tab at https://btw.bitwrap.io is playing: the program ends and whatever its lines held (a filter, a mute) is put back. Reaches every live tab of the token's account, or one tab by session (the id the page's MCP panel shows). Needs a bearer token. No tab connected: a no_session error that says how to connect one.

device.description: Id of one of your paired phones (djrust on Android), from the devices tool. Targets that phone alone; do not combine with session.

session.description: Session id of one browser tab, from the MCP panel of the page. Leave out to use your own signed-in tabs (every live one for eval/load/stop, the latest for get).
